chunks: We said: As for that which indicates its veracity, the Shia Imamiyah narrate it in the manner of Tawatur (consecutive transmission) from predecessor to successor, and the method of validating this is found in the books of the Imamiyah.

The texts regarding Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) follow a single method. Furthermore, the narration by the two differing sects, which are distinct in belief, indicates the correctness of what they agreed to narrate, because custom dictates that whoever believes in a doctrine for which the path to its authenticity is established, their motivations will be abundant to narrate it, and the motivations of their opponent will be abundant to invalidate what they narrated, or to criticize it and reject its narration. Customs are established in praising men, criticizing them, honoring them, and diminishing them. When we see the opposing faction to this faction having narred the same as they narred, without subjecting it to criticism regarding its narration, nor denying its content, this indicates that God Almighty took charge of its narration and compelled them to narrate it; and this is proof of the correctness of what the report contained. As for the proof that the Imams (peace be upon them) are intended by these reports and what is meant by them, it is that when it is established by these reports that the Imamate is restricted to the Twelve Imams, and that they neither increase nor decrease, that which we have gone to is established, because the Ummah is between two sayers: one who considers the number we mentioned, he says that what is meant by it is he who goes to his Imamate, and he who opposes their Imamate does not consider this number; so the saying with considering the number that the intended ones are others is an exit from consensus (Ijma), and that which leads to that necessitates saying its invalidity.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful, a title for Imam Ali (peace be upon him)
key_terms.الإِمَامَةَ: Imamate, the leadership and spiritual authority of the Imams
key_terms.التَّوَاتُرِ: Consecutive transmission, a method of narration ensuring authenticity

ai.seo_question: What are the proofs for the authenticity of the tradition of the Twelve Imams in Shia theology?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi employs the principle of *Tawatur* (mass transmission) and cross-sectarian agreement (*tawatur al-ghayr*) to validate the tradition of the Twelve Imams, arguing that the consistency of opposing groups in transmitting the same report indicates divine preservation. He further deduces that since the Imamate is numerically fixed at twelve, any deviation from this specific count or the rejection of their authority falls outside the bounds of Islamic consensus (*Ijma*), thereby establishing the infallibility and exclusive legitimacy of the Ahl al-Bayt.
